decisions.reason: As a very recent launch with no visible failure signal and a clear link to the firm's flooring business, management would likely keep it for another year while monitoring whether sales meet emerging aspiration levels.
Maintenance oil fits closely with wooden floor use and, under bounded rationality with limited post-launch evidence, an established firm would usually continue it unless results clearly fall short.
This care product complements oiled wood floors and would likely be retained because the firm has little performance history yet and can use organisational slack to learn from the market.
A moisture-protection underlay is a plausible accessory to the firm's flooring offer, so absent clear underperformance management would keep it as part of a broader product system.
High-density underlay foam is adjacent to the core flooring assortment and would likely stay on the market while the firm compares its acceptance with internal expectations and peer offerings.

Oak parquet flooring is the closest to the firm's core wood-products capabilities, so a mature German manufacturer would be least likely to drop it after only one year without strong negative feedback.
